score_note: Based on the number and severity of open findings. {n} finding(s) to confirm not counted.
audit_approach: targeted review of sensitive areas, without altering data.
every finding independently re-checked, CVSS 4.0 rating.
ai_note: The analysis was assisted by an AI model (Claude, Anthropic), with independent verification of every finding.
standards: Standards: OWASP Top 10 (2021), OWASP ASVS 4.0, CWE Top 25, CVSS 4.0, ANSSI guidelines.
local_note: The target is a local development environment. Production settings (TLS, DNS, headers set by the hosting provider) may differ and were not assessed.
scale_intro: CVSS 4.0 base scores (FIRST). The severity may be adjusted for business impact; any adjustment is justified in the finding.
scale_rows: Simple remote exploitation, full compromise or massive data leak.
Significant impact on data or service, realistic exploitation.
Exploitation under specific conditions, or limited impact.
Good practice or observation with no direct risk.
no_findings: No vulnerability was found in the scope.
business_adjustment: Severity adjusted for business impact from {from} to {to}: {why}
plan_medium: Medium term · 3 months · Harden and monitor
audit_glossary: standard 0–10 score that measures the technical severity of a vulnerability. This report uses version 4.0, published by FIRST.
public identifier of a known vulnerability.
foundation that publishes the reference web security standards.
audit_disclaimer: This report reflects the state of the scope on the audit dates. It is strictly confidential and intended solely for the client named at the top. Testing was carried out with the client's written authorisation, without altering production data.
evidence_intro: Every source was copied before analysis; its SHA-256 fingerprint proves it has not been altered since.
read_only_note: Read-only analysis: nothing on the system was modified or restarted. Log contents are treated as untrusted data.
traces: Traces to look for and remove
ioc_intro: Use these to check that nothing is left behind, here or on other sites on the same hosting. Any secrets found are truncated.
defang_note: Malicious URLs and domains are defanged (hxxp, [.]) to prevent accidental clicks.
flaws_made_possible: The flaws that made the attack possible
rem_containment: Containment · immediate · Cut off the attacker
rem_eradication: Eradication · 24 to 72 h · Clean up and fix
rem_note: These actions are recommendations. Unless stated otherwise, none of them was carried out as part of this analysis.
gdpr_points: **Article 33**: a personal data breach that poses a risk to individuals must be notified to the supervisory authority (in France, the CNIL) within 72 hours of becoming aware of it.
**Article 34**: if the risk is high, the people affected must also be informed.
Every breach, even when not notified, must be recorded in the breach register.
gdpr_decision: The decision to notify lies with the data controller, {controller}. This report provides the technical facts needed for that decision and is not legal advice. CNIL online notification: notifications.cnil.fr.
incident_glossary: hidden file or access left by an attacker to get back into the system.
technical trace (IP address, file, account) that signals an intrusion.
unique signature of a file: the slightest change alters it completely.
0–10 score that measures the severity of a vulnerability. This report uses version 4.0, published by FIRST.
incident_disclaimer: This report reflects what was known when it was written, based on the evidence listed in section 02. It is strictly confidential and intended solely for the client named at the top. The analysis was carried out with the client's authorisation, read-only, without altering production data.
